decision: Does this copy persuade with true claims, or does it use manipulative patterns that must be cut or have a fact confirmed?
limitations: It matches wording patterns. It cannot tell whether a scarcity, urgency or social-proof claim is true; a VERIFY flag means someone must confirm the fact, not that the claim is fine.
A PASS means no listed pattern matched, not that the copy is honest or will convert. Manipulative copy worded outside its patterns passes.
It checks copy only. It does not diagnose which friction (attention, comprehension, belief, value, risk, inertia) is blocking the buyer; that diagnosis comes first.
Anything passed is read as copy, so JSON or a mistyped flag such as --fiel is checked as text and returns PASS rather than an error; check the result quotes your draft.
review: Whoever owns the page confirms every VERIFY claim (seat counts, deadlines, customer numbers) is literally true before it ships. Legal checks any auto-renewal or trial-to-paid wording the engine flags.
